properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 2:45PM MDT until July 29 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Elbert County in east central Colorado...
Southeastern Arapahoe County in northeastern Colorado...
Douglas County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 245 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Middle Garber Creek, Rainbow Creek, Jackson Creek, Garber Creek,
Cook Creek, East Cherry Creek, West Creek, Indian Creek, Deep
Creek, Spring Creek, Camp Creek, Gove Creek, Murphy Creek, Newlin
Gulch, East Plum Creek, Sugar Creek, Trout Creek, Horse Creek,
Cherry Creek, Bear Creek, Carpenter Creek, Big Dry Creek, Piney
Creek, Running Creek, North Garber Creek, Pine Creek, Coal Creek,
Kinney Creek, West Toll Gate Creek, Willow Creek, Plum Creek,
Antelope Creek, Bayou Gulch, First Creek, Watson Park Creek, Dry
Gulch, Happy Canyon Creek, Lake Gulch, South Platte River and
East Toll Gate Creek. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1
inch are expected over the area. This additional rain will result
in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Southern Aurora, eastern Centennial, Castle Rock, Parker, Lone
Tree, Larkspur, Castle Pines, Franktown, Sedalia, The Pinery,
Perry Park, Ponderosa Park, Devil's Head, Arapahoe Park,
Foxfield, Castlewood Canyon and Shamballa.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 2:44PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 243 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Greenhorn Mountain, or 29 miles southwest of Pueblo. This
thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, nickel size hail and torrential
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Rye and Colorado City.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 2:39PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 237 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Victor, or 19 miles southwest of Colorado Springs, moving south at 10
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, penny size hail and torrential
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Heavy rainfall could cause flash flooding,
washouts, and excessive flows in area creeks, and streams.
A Flash Flood Warning is effect for much of this area
through 530 PM.

Locations impacted include...
Victor.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 2:31PM MDT until July 29 at 5:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Teller County in central Colorado...

* Until 530 PM MDT.

* At 231 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, rural roads
and normally dry washes, as well as other poor drainage
and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Victor.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Beaver Creek, Middle Beaver Creek, Wilson Creek and their
tributaries.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 2:20PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 217 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 10
miles north of Royal Gorge, or 33 miles southwest of Colorado
Springs. This thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, brief half inch hail and
torrential rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Heavy rainfall could cause ponding of water on
paved road surfaces, washouts on dirt roads, and quick
runoff causing high flows in area creeks, streams and
normally dry washouts.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of north central
Fremont County over the Wilson Creek centered around 10 miles north
of Royal Gorge.
